turns.prompt:
Bootstrap a game jam repo for a mobile-first browser game using Phaser 3, deployed on Netlify.

Constraints:
- No build step, no npm, no bundler. Plain ES modules served as static files.
- Load Phaser from a CDN (jsdelivr, pinned to a specific 3.x version) in index.html.
- Must run as-is on any static host, so use relative paths only.
- Phone is the primary target: touch controls first, keyboard as a bonus on laptop.

Structure:
- index.html: viewport meta (no zoom), full-screen canvas, Phaser script tag, loads src/main.js
- src/main.js: Phaser game config with Scale.FIT + CENTER_BOTH, a fixed logical resolution (portrait 720x1280 unless I say otherwise), arcade physics, and the scene list
- src/scenes/: BootScene (generates placeholder textures in code with Graphics, no image files), MenuScene (tap to start), GameScene (a tiny playable demo: a player that moves toward where you touch or drag, plus something to collect, plus a score), GameOverScene (tap to restart)
- src/config.js: tunable constants (speeds, sizes, colors) in one place, so I can ask for "feel" changes quickly
- assets/: empty folder with a .gitkeep, for later
- netlify.toml: publish = "." with no build command; add a header rule so index.html and src/** are served with Cache-Control: no-cache (so the phone always picks up the latest push)
- README.md: how to play locally (any static server, e.g. `python3 -m http.server`) and a note that Netlify deploys on push

Also create CLAUDE.md with working rules for future sessions:
- Keep it no-build and CDN-only. Don't add npm dependencies.
- Every change must keep the game playable on a phone. Touch input is the primary control scheme.
- Placeholder art is drawn in
turns.reply:
The repo is set up and pushed to `ccr-f83e2812-i8p69i`. I played it in a headless browser set up like a phone (390×844 with touch), and a full round works: tap to start, drag to move, collect a coin and the score goes up, get hit and see Game Over, tap to restart. No console errors.

**Your message was cut off** at "Placeholder art is drawn in…". I finished that rule as: placeholder art is drawn in code in `BootScene`, and when real art arrives it goes in `assets/` and is loaded under the same texture names, so the scenes don't change. If you meant something else, tell me the rest and I'll update `CLAUDE.md`.

What's in it:
- **`index.html`**: zoom is disabled, the canvas fills the screen, and scrolling, pull-to-refresh and long-press menus are switched off. It loads Phaser **3.90.0** from jsdelivr (the newest 3.x release, and the link works) and then `./src/main.js`.
- **`src/main.js`**: portrait 720×1280, `Scale.FIT` + `CENTER_BOTH`, arcade physics, and the scene list Boot → Menu → Game → GameOver.
- **`src/config.js`**: all the tunable numbers in one place, including player speed and how quickly it reacts, coin size, how often the red balls spawn and how fast they fall, and the colors.
- **The scenes**:
  - **Boot** draws the circles you see in code.
  - **Menu** is "tap to start".
  - **Game**: you hold a finger down and the player glides toward it, slowing as it gets close. You collect the yellow coins for points and avoid the red balls falling from the top, which get faster as your score rises. Arrow keys and WASD also work on a laptop.
  - **GameOver** shows your score and your best score, which is saved in the browser.
- **`netlify.toml`**: serves the repo root as-is with no build. The page and everything under `src/` are sent with `Cache-Control: no-cache`, so a reload on the phone gets the latest push.
- **`README.md`** and **`CLAUDE.md`** as you asked, plus `assets/.gitkeep`.

Additions you didn't ask for:
- **Red balls** that end the run, so the Game Over screen has a reason to appear.
- **A short shake and phone vibration** when you're hit.
- **Taps are ignored for 0.4 seconds on the Game Over screen**, so the same tap that killed you doesn't restart the game instantly.

**Deploys:** Netlify usually publishes only one branch (normally `main`), so this branch probably won't go live until you merge it.

turns.prompt: Should also keep a record of all ai use for development. All human prompts, basic metadata (when sent, if possible how many tokens/claude quota was used). At the end of the project, i want to have a nicely scrollable making-of, a way for people to see exactly how it was built, and an understanding how much it cost - so people feel they could do something like this themselves
turns.reply:
I've set up the AI-use log and the making-of page, and pushed both to the existing pull request (#1).

**What's recorded:** every human prompt word for word with the time it was sent, Claude's final reply (progress notes folded underneath), how long Claude worked, which tools it used, tokens read and written, and the commits made in that turn. Tool output, system prompts and Claude's hidden reasoning are left out.

**Where it comes from:** Claude Code already writes a log of each session inside the cloud container, with exact token counts. A new script, `tools/ai_log.py`, turns that into one file per session under `making-of/sessions/`. That matters because the log disappears when the container is thrown away, so it has to be saved into the repo as we go. Two things keep it current:
- `CLAUDE.md` now tells Claude to run the script before the last commit of every turn, even when no code changed.
- A hook in `.claude/settings.json` also runs it automatically each time you send a prompt.

**The making-of page:** it's at `/making-of/` on the deployed site. It's a phone-friendly timeline with totals at the top: prompts sent, cost, time Claude spent working, commits and tokens. Each prompt card shows your message, Claude's reply, the cost and the running total so far, and links to the commits. I checked it in a phone-sized headless browser in light and dark mode: no console errors and no sideways scrolling.

**Cost so far:** about **$2.46** across the 3 prompts, with Claude working about 6 minutes in total. That's what the same tokens would cost at Anthropic's public API prices. I checked the formula against Claude Code's own cost record for the first prompt and they matched.

**Limitations:**
- **Subscription quota isn't available.** Your plan's usage isn't in the logs, so the page shows the API-equivalent price instead. There's a note in `making-of/meta.json` explaining that on a subscription you pay a flat monthly fee; edit it to name your plan if you like.
- **Each turn's ending is saved one turn late.** The save happens just before the final commit, so a turn's final reply and last few tokens are only picked up on your next prompt. If a session ends without another prompt, its last reply won't be in the log. This turn's reply will appear after your next message.
- **The prompts will be public.** Once this is merged and deployed, everything you type to Claude in this repo is visible on the live site, so don't paste secrets into prompts.

turns.prompt: Is there any other way to get the plan limit, eg checking some claude code api at start/end of turns/sessions? Im on a 10x max plan
turns.reply:
Yes. Cloud sessions record your real plan usage in their event stream, and the making-of page now tracks it per prompt. That's pushed to pull request #1.

**Where it comes from:** at the start of each turn, Claude Code logs a rate-limit event with your utilization of both Max limits. That's the 5-hour rolling window and the weekly limit, each with its reset time. These events aren't saved anywhere in the container, but I can read them with the cloud session's `list_events` tool.

**How it's captured:**
- **Fetching:** `CLAUDE.md` now tells Claude to call that tool at the start of every turn. It's a small call, about 20 events filtered to just the rate-limit ones.
- **Saving:** the tool's result lands in the local transcript, and `tools/ai_log.py` picks it up from there. Snapshots are also kept in the session files, so nothing is lost when the container is thrown away.

**Readings for this project so far:**

| Prompt | 5-hour window at start | Weekly limit at start |
|---|---|---|
| #1 bootstrap (Oct 7) | 1% | 31% |
| #2 auto PR | 3% | 32% |
| #3 making-of | 5% | 32% |
| #4 this one | 6% | 32% |

So building the game, the log and this page has used about 1% of your weekly Max (10x) limit so far. At API list prices the same tokens would cost about $3.32.

**On the page:** a new totals tile shows the share of the weekly limit used. Each prompt card shows how much of each limit went up before the next prompt, for example "plan +1% of 5h · 0% of week". `making-of/meta.json` now names your plan.

**Limitations:**
- **Only 1% steps.** Small prompts often show +0%; the total across the project is the more meaningful number.
- **Account-wide.** The limits cover all your Claude use, so a claude.ai chat or another session at the same time gets counted against whichever prompt was running.
- **Cloud sessions only.** The event stream exists only in cloud sessions. In a local Claude Code CLI session there's nothing to read, so those prompts get token and cost figures but no plan figures.
- **This prompt's own figure arrives late.** Like the reply text, it's filled in once you send the next prompt.

turns.prompt: Yes, should be smart about filtering the limit usage. There is concurrent work going on. Should check the limit at the start/end of working sessions here
turns.reply:
Your concurrent work is now filtered out of the plan-usage numbers in two ways. The changes are pushed to pull request #1, and the page still renders cleanly on a phone.

**How the readings work:** this session only gets a plan-usage reading when one of its own requests sees the account's usage change. I confirmed that by starting a tiny helper agent mid-turn, which produced a fresh reading straight away. So usage from your other work while this session sits idle only shows up in the first reading of the next prompt.

**1. Idle time between prompts is never counted.** Each prompt now gets a start reading, taken just after Claude's first response, and an end reading from its last activity. Only the change between those two counts. The jump from 37% to 43% between earlier prompts now falls in a gap and is ignored.

**2. Spikes during a prompt are checked against its cost.** The page works out an average "% of limit per dollar of tokens" across all prompts. If a prompt's usage jumped well beyond what its own token cost explains, it's shown crossed out as "concurrent use, not counted" and left out of the total. I tested this on made-up data: a +6% spike on a $0.50 prompt was dropped, while +1% and +2% changes on $2–3 prompts were kept.

**Start and end checks:** `CLAUDE.md` now has Claude check the readings at the start of every prompt and again just before the final commit.

**Result so far:** the page shows **<1%** of your weekly Max (10x) limit used by this project, against $8.62 at API prices. Readings only move in whole percent, so individual prompts mostly show +0%. The total becomes more meaningful as the jam goes on.

**Remaining gap:** concurrent work that happens during a prompt and stays small, about 1% or less, can't be told apart from this project's own usage, so it still counts.
